root_idea.summary: The root centers on tender compassion and emotional yearning, often directed toward a person, offspring, homeland, or object of affection.
root_idea.development: The same emotional orientation may be expressed with a yearning or plaintive sound; from this develop terms for mercy, affectionate care, cries, resonant sounds, and objects characterized by such sounds.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized noun citation form حَنَانٌ; the Quranic occurrence is the accusative حَنَانًا.

senses.definition: Mercy, tender compassion, or affectionate care.
senses.usage_conditions: In وَحَنَانًا مِنْ لَدُنَّا (19:13), the word denotes mercy bestowed by God, with tenderness and affection as part of its emotional nuance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To yearn, long for, or desire; to be emotionally moved with grief or joy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, the heart, an animal, or other subject. A camel or pigeon may yearn toward its young or home, often with a cry; the heart may yearn without producing a sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To emit a plaintive, resonant, creaking, or ringing sound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transferred use applied to a lute, reed, bow, basin, mast, wind, or similar object; the sound may be associated with grief, liveliness, or yearning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show mercy, compassion, pity, or affectionate inclination toward someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction حَنَّ عَلَيْهِ takes the object with عَلَى; it is also used of an animal's compassionate inclination toward its young.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn away, shun, or turn someone or something away or back.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: With عَنْ, حَنَّ denotes turning away or avoiding; the transitive حَنَّهُ denotes causing someone or something to turn away or back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become possessed by a demon and hence become mad or insane.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare reported usage, with مَحْنُونٌ used for a person so affected.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause someone to become merciful, compassionate, pitiful, or favourably inclined.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical explanation is reported as current usage and possibly also Classical Arabic.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attack or charge and then retreat cowardly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic use describing a person who makes an assault and withdraws.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Not to turn away, leave, or relinquish; of a mark, not to disappear from the skin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported in constructions such as مَا حَنَّنَ عَنِّي; the related wording and reading are presented as variant usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a tree or herb, to blossom or flower.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used intransitively of vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a bow twang or give a sound by pulling and releasing its string.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is the bow, with the sound resulting from release of the drawn string.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do wrong, make a mistake, or miss the object aimed at.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate reported Form IV usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be intensely affected by longing, especially longing for one's homeland.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction استحنّهُ الشوقُ إلى وطنه presents longing as the force producing the emotional effect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A class or tribe of jinn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions vary: they are identified as beings preceding Adam, the lowest or weakest kind of jinn, associated with black dogs, or creatures between jinn and humankind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Likeness or resemblance, especially resemblance inherited from a parent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Preserved in proverbial expressions about a child or person resembling a parent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The grumbling or yearning cry of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for a camel's vocalization.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man's wife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An independently attested nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Demoniacal possession, madness, or insanity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression بِهِ حِنَّةٌ, ‘he has demoniacal possession or madness.’

other_classical_meanings.definition: Provision, blessing, or good bestowed by God.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical extension distinct from the Quranic mercy sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quality inspiring reverence, respect, or honour; gravity or sedateness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's dignified or venerable bearing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Evil or mischief that continues for a long time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct, rarely attested nominal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wind that makes a plaintive or moaning sound like the yearning of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival noun applied specifically to wind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who marries from tenderness or compassion for her young children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The stated motive is that the husband will support the children.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Yearning, longing, or desire, especially an affectionate yearning accompanied by pity or compassion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may also denote the leaning or inclination of a palm trunk; it can be used of longing toward offspring or homeland.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cry or sound expressing yearning, grief, joy, or another lively emotion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may be a camel's yearning cry or a sound from the bosom during weeping; distinctions are reported between this and the nasal sound called خَنِينٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for one of the months of Jumādā.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported usages identify it with Jumādā al-awwālā, Jumādā al-ākhirah, or the month named by the tribe of ʿĀd; variant plurals are also recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The proper name of a known place, as in the Quranic expression يوم حنين, ‘the day of Hunayn.’
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This proper-name use is distinct from the common noun حَنِينٌ and from its month-name usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Belonging to the jinn called الحِنّ; especially, a dog of that group.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the phrase كَلْبٌ حِنِّيٌّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who yearns, longs for, or desires something and inclines toward it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may describe a person or, figuratively, an object characterized by yearning or its sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who yearns for a former husband or for her child or children.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions include grieving tenderness for children, yearning for a former husband, or marrying after divorce while continuing to yearn for him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow that twangs or makes a sound when its string is released.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun or epithet motivated by the bow's characteristic sound.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet for something producing or associated with a plaintive or yearning sound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a lute, clouds, an arrow, a strenuous journey involving yearning camels, or a conspicuous road associated with the cries of camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who shows favour or a favourable aspect to someone who turns away or shuns him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized personal description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Merciful or having mercy; the Merciful as a divine epithet.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical epithet and reported name of God, distinct in form from the Quranic noun حَنَانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Henna, Lawsonia inermis; a dialectal form of حِنَّاءٌ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or variant botanical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The flower of the henna plant, or the flower of a tree or plant generally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A singulative botanical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Yearning, longing, desiring, or affected by an intense emotion of grief or joy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form may describe a person or an animal characterized by yearning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel characterized by yearning toward her young.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized feminine form derived from the animal's yearning behavior.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One affected by intense longing for his homeland.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The related form مُسْتَحِنٌّ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possessed, mad, or affected by epilepsy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man; explanations include possession by a jinn, insanity, or an epileptic seizure followed by temporary recovery.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Yearning and transferred sound uses are represented separately.
Causative compassion sense, retained with its qualification.
Doing wrong or missing an aim.
Longing as the cause of intense emotion.
Wind with a camel-like plaintive sound.
Woman marrying from tenderness for children.
Yearning person, specialized feminine form, bow, and sound-associated epithets.
Flower of henna or other plants.
She-camel and one affected by longing for home.

cautions: The supplied QAC form set contains only حَنَانٌ; the separately attested proper-name use حُنَيْنٌ is retained as a Classical lexical item because Mufradat discusses it but no corresponding QAC form group is supplied.

Several Classical branches are reported as variants, attributed usages, or tentative explanations; those qualifications are preserved in their usage conditions rather than treated as ordinary Quranic senses.
